items.description: Resting energy expenditure REE = 10 W + 6.25 H - 5 A + s (W kg, H cm, A years; s = +5 men, -161 women)
items.note: Predicts measured REE within +/-10% for about 80% of non-obese adults. 1 kcal = 4184 J.

items.description: Physical activity level PAL = total daily energy expenditure / BMR
items.note: PAL above about 2.4 cannot be sustained for long periods.

items.description: Maximum sustained (weeks to months) total energy expenditure
Metabolic equivalents of activities (1 MET = 1 kcal/kg/h, about resting rate)
items.note: Ranges span the Compendium codes for each activity at light-to-vigorous effort. Gold panning has no Compendium code; its range is taken from standing-in-stream and moderate manual work codes (low confidence).

items.description: Adequate intake of total water (drinks plus food water), adults 19-50, temperate climate
items.note: Heavy work in heat raises losses to 6-12 L/day (Adolph 1947).

items.description: Survival time without any water intake
items.note: About 3-5 days at rest in a temperate climate; under 2 days with exertion in heat; death at roughly 15-25% body-mass water loss.

items.description: Survival time in total starvation with water available, initially normal-weight adult
items.note: 1981 Maze hunger strikers died after 46-73 days; obese subjects survive far longer, limited by protein loss.

items.description: Intrinsic (free-running) period of the human circadian pacemaker under forced desynchrony
items.note: Mean 24.15 h (SD ~0.2 h, n = 157; Duffy et al. 2011); Czeisler et al. (1999) report 24.18 h. Women average ~6 min shorter than men.

items.description: Range of light-dark cycle periods to which the human clock can entrain under ordinary light levels
items.note: Under 20 h and 28 h days (and a fortiori 36 h) the clock free-runs and sleep and alertness desynchronise (Czeisler et al. 1999).

items.description: Maximum phase shift from a single bright-light pulse (6.7 h, ~10,000 lux)
items.note: Ordinary daylight exposure shifts the clock about 1 h per day (re-entrainment after jet lag ~1 day per time zone).

items.description: Comfortable walking speed of healthy adults aged 20-59
items.note: Declines to about 1.2-1.3 m/s in the 70s.

items.description: Naismith's rule for hill walking time: 1 h per 5 km horizontal plus 1 h per 600 m of ascent
Load as a fraction of body mass that can be carried on long marches without excessive injury risk
items.note: About one third of body mass for sustained marching; loads above ~45% sharply raise injury and energy cost.

items.description: Illuminance at the eye of ordinary indoor room light in the evening
items.note: The room-light condition of Gooley et al. (2011) was < 200 lux against < 3 lux dim light; 200 lux is its upper bound. Room light before bedtime suppressed melatonin and delayed its onset by ~90 min against dim light.
